y-m-25-08.topic: Range where linear-function model holds: when situation change, equation change too

y-m-25-08.s.s1.prompt: Information about tank draining come one piece at a time. At each step choose the thought wey fit best.

y-m-25-06.title: If areas same, slopes same too?
y-m-25-06.topic: Triangle formed by graph of linear function and both axes: same area, different slopes
y-m-25-06.goal: Use counterexample to reject general statement “same areas mean same slopes”, and work out how conclusion change if condition change.
y-m-25-06.material: On coordinate plane, line get x-intercept a and y-intercept b (a and b no be 0). E pass through (a, 0) and (0, b), making triangle with x-axis and y-axis. Triangle area na half times absolute a times absolute b. Hyeonu say, “Lines making triangles with same area against the two axes must have same slope.”
y-m-25-06.prereq.0: Wetin x-intercept, y-intercept, and slope mean on linear function graph
y-m-25-06.s.s1.prompt: You wan test if Hyeonu statement “lines making same area triangles with axes get same slope” always true. What two lines you need find to show statement wrong?
y-m-25-06.s.s1.hint.0: Write separately the “condition” (areas same) and “conclusion” (slopes same) in Hyeonu statement.
y-m-25-06.s.s1.hint.1: Say what example would keep condition but break conclusion.
y-m-25-06.s.s1.o.a: Two lines with different areas and same slope
y-m-25-06.s.s1.r.a: You reverse direction of the claim (slope to area).
y-m-25-06.s.s1.o.b: Two lines with same area and same slope
y-m-25-06.s.s1.r.b: You forget finding an example where claim works only confirm am.
y-m-25-06.s.s1.o.c: Two lines with same area and different slopes
y-m-25-06.s.s1.r.c: You see one example with condition true and conclusion false na counterexample.
y-m-25-06.s.s1.o.d: Two lines with different areas and different slopes
y-m-25-06.s.s1.r.d: You forget example where condition (same area) not true no test the claim.
y-m-25-06.s.s1.explain: To break “if A, then B” always true, one example wey satisfy A but break B enough. Here na two lines with same area but different slopes.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 lines whose triangle area 12 and whose slopes all different. For each line, enter x-intercept a and y-intercept b. For now, a and b both positive.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.hint.0: First write as expression wetin a and b must give for area to be 12.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.hint.1: Choose a first and adjust b; check yourself say slopes no overlap.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.fail.c1: a and b no both positive.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.fail.c2: Triangle area (half the product of a and b) no be 12.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.explain: Example: (4, 6), (6, 4), (3, 8). All get area 12 but slopes different: −3/2, −2/3, −8/3. So Hyeonu statement no always true.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.prompt: Answer Hyeonu in one or two sentences, using examples as evidence.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.hint.0: You fit use intercepts from both lines you make above.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.hint.1: First write one sentence “why Hyeonu statement wrong”.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You check say your examples get same area but different slopes?
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You write knowing one example enough?
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You explain how the word “always” fail?
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.model.0: Hyeonu statement wrong. For example, if a=4 and b=6, area na 12; if a=6, b=4, area still 12 but slopes different.
y-m-25-06.s.s2.because.model.1: No always. Line with intercepts (4, 6) and line with (3, 8) both get area 12 but different slopes, so counterexample.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.prompt: Now change the condition. How many lines get slope −3/2 (read “negative three halves”) and make triangle with axes area 12? This time, no assume both intercepts positive.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.hint.0: Write line with slope −3/2 as y=−(3/2)x+k, and find where e meet both axes for k=6 and k=−6.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.hint.1: Find triangle area in both cases and check if e be 12.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.o.a: One: only line with intercepts (4, 0) and (0, 6), nothing else
y-m-25-06.s.s3.r.a: You carry over positive-intercept assumption from previous step.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.o.b: Two: one line with positive intercepts and one with negative intercepts
y-m-25-06.s.s3.r.b: You notice line with negative intercepts can get same area too.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.o.c: None: because when slope fixed, area fixed too
y-m-25-06.s.s3.r.c: You think slope alone fix area.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.o.d: Unlimited: any line fit work if slope same
y-m-25-06.s.s3.r.d: You no consider how many lines area condition allow.
y-m-25-06.s.s3.explain: A line with slope −3/2 get form y=−(3/2)x+k. Area na k²/3; for area 12, k=6 or −6. So 2 lines: y=−(3/2)x+6 and y=−(3/2)x−6.

y-m-25-02.title: Wetin measurements we need to predict spring length?
y-m-25-02.topic: Find the equation of a linear function: are the measurement records enough, and within what range fit we trust a prediction?
y-m-25-02.goal: Judge what information we need to find the equation of a linear function, and say how far we fit trust a prediction from that equation.
y-m-25-02.material: For science class, you hang weights on a spring and measure the spring's total length. Let weight be x g and total spring length be y cm. For this spring, up to 250 g, y na linear function of x, y=ax+b (a no be zero). Assume all measurements use the same spring with no error. Mina get different groups' measurement records.
y-m-25-02.thinking.1: Decide for yourself what information we need
y-m-25-02.thinking.2: Know the range where the equation work
y-m-25-02.prereq.0: Wetin a and b mean in linear function y=ax+b
y-m-25-02.prereq.1: Read coordinates of a point on coordinate plane
y-m-25-02.s.s1.prompt: From the records below, choose all sets where that set alone fit determine one equation y=ax+b for this spring. Nothing else known apart from each record.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.hint.0: For each record set, count how many different weights dey.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.hint.1: Write each set as points (weight, length) and imagine how many straight lines pass through all the points.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.o.a: The case with only one record: 10 cm at 0 g
y-m-25-02.s.s1.r.a: Maybe you no notice say one point fit have several lines passing through am.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.o.b: 12 cm at 50 g, 14 cm at 100 g
y-m-25-02.s.s1.r.b: Na judgment wey look how much length change between 2 different weights.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.o.c: One measurement of 14 cm at 100 g, repeated twice (14 cm both times)
y-m-25-02.s.s1.r.c: Na judgment wey think many measurements enough. You no count how many different weights dey.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.o.d: 12 cm at 50 g, 16 cm at 150 g
y-m-25-02.s.s1.r.d: Na judgment wey notice records at two weights far apart also show the change.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.o.e: 10 cm at 0 g, 18 cm at 200 g
y-m-25-02.s.s1.r.e: Na judgment wey notice the length with no weight too fit serve as one point.
y-m-25-02.s.s1.explain: The equation of a linear function get one fixed answer if records dey for 2 points with different x. If there only one point, or the same weight measured plenty times, several lines fit pass through the point, so we no fit determine am.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.prompt: The records in b, d, and e all give same equation y=0.04x+10 (x in g, y in cm). The spring manual only say “up to 250 g, length na linear function of weight”. Mina put x=300 inside this equation and predict y=22 cm. How we suppose treat this prediction?
y-m-25-02.s.s2.hint.0: Compare the weight range in the manual with the weight wey you wan predict.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.hint.1: Think separately about the range confirmed by experiment or manual, and the range wey no confirm.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.o.a: I calculate am with the equation, so e fine to write say at 300 g the length na 22 cm
y-m-25-02.s.s2.r.a: You trust the value as e be without checking the range where the equation work.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.o.b: E pass the range in the manual, so I think we no fit use this equation at all
y-m-25-02.s.s2.r.b: You throw away the whole equation without separating values outside the range from values inside.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.o.c: Say outside 250 g no guarantee dey, so 22 cm na only prediction
y-m-25-02.s.s2.r.c: You talk separately about the range wey equation confirm and the range wey e no confirm.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.o.d: E only pass 250 g small, so the error go small and e fine to write 22 cm
y-m-25-02.s.s2.r.d: You think say small difference no matter, but nobody give reason for that.
y-m-25-02.s.s2.explain: The equation get guarantee only inside the confirmed range. For value pass 250 g, na prediction under condition “if this equation continue to work”. For values inside the range, like 120 g, you fit predict with the equation.
y-m-25-02.s.s3.prompt: The group with the first records (only one record, 10 cm at 0 g) fit do exactly one more measurement. Write what to measure so we fit find the equation, and why that measurement help.
y-m-25-02.s.s3.hint.0: Think what go change if you measure at weight different from the weight of the point you already get.
y-m-25-02.s.s3.hint.1: Write the difference in weight and length between both points.
y-m-25-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: The new weight you measure different from 0 g?
y-m-25-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write why that measurement help?
y-m-25-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You say exactly which values we need, weight and length?
y-m-25-02.s.s3.model.0: Hang a weight different from 0 g, like 100 g, and measure the length. Then we get 2 points, so we fit find how much length increase when weight increase, that is the slope.
y-m-25-02.s.s3.model.1: Hang one more weight at a weight different from 0 g and measure the length. Compare how much length change with how much the weight change to find the slope.

y-m-25-07.title: What values a and b need so line no pass through second quadrant?
y-m-25-07.topic: Quadrants a linear function graph pass through, and slope/y-intercept signs
y-m-25-07.goal: Use slope and y-intercept signs to find when line no pass second quadrant, and remember boundary case where y-intercept na 0.
y-m-25-07.material: Graph y=ax+b na line (a no be 0). a na slope and b na y-intercept. Second quadrant na points with negative x and positive y. Points on x-axis or y-axis no belong to any quadrant.
y-m-25-07.prereq.0: Wetin slope and y-intercept mean for y=ax+b
y-m-25-07.prereq.1: Where quadrants dey (second quadrant: x<0, y>0)
y-m-25-07.s.s1.prompt: Choose all lines below wey no pass second quadrant.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.hint.0: For each equation, calculate y when x=−1 and x=−10.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.hint.1: Find a place where y become positive even when x negative.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.r.a: You remember position of line with positive slope and negative y-intercept.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.r.b: You think say if y-intercept negative, line going upper-left avoid second quadrant too.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.r.c: You miss say if y-intercept positive, even moving left, line still above.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.r.d: You think line through origin no pass any quadrant.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.r.e: You know line through origin still pass through one pair of quadrants.
y-m-25-07.s.s1.explain: Second quadrant na x<0, y>0. For y=3x−2 and y=2x, y negative (or 0) when x negative, so dem no enter second quadrant. For other lines, y become positive somewhere with x negative.
y-m-25-07.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different (a, b) pairs for y=ax+b wey no pass second quadrant. a slope, b y-intercept.
y-m-25-07.s.s2.hint.0: Make slope positive, change y-intercept, and check if y become positive when x=−1 and −10.
y-m-25-07.s.s2.fail.c1: With this slope, y become positive somewhere when x small enough, or e no be linear function. Check slope sign again.
y-m-25-07.s.s2.fail.c2: Y-intercept too big, so a little left from y-axis still got positive y. Check y-intercept range again.
y-m-25-07.s.s2.explain: Example: (3, −2), (2, 0), (0.5, −4). If slope positive and y-intercept 0 or less, line pass only first and third quadrants (and fourth too if y-intercept negative).
y-m-25-07.s.s3.prompt: One student summarize above result with reasons. Choose wrong line (line numbers start at 1 as shown on screen).
y-m-25-07.s.s3.hint.0: Check line with b=0, for example y=2x, where x negative.
y-m-25-07.s.s3.hint.1: Among examples you make in step 2, find one wey no match this summary.
y-m-25-07.s.s3.line.0: If a<0, y become positive somewhere when x small enough, so line pass second quadrant. So a must be >0.
y-m-25-07.s.s3.line.1: If a>0 and b>0, move small distance left from (0,b), y still positive, so line pass second quadrant.
y-m-25-07.s.s3.line.2: If b=0, line pass origin, but then no y-intercept, so only b<0 possible.
y-m-25-07.s.s3.line.3: Summary: it no pass second quadrant only when a>0 and b<0.
y-m-25-07.s.s3.explain: Lines 3 and 4 wrong. Line through origin still get y-intercept 0 (b=0). If a>0 and b=0, line no pass second quadrant. So summary must be a>0 and b≤0.

y-m-25-01.title: Bike rental plans: which one cheap pass?
y-m-25-01.topic: Apply linear functions: the time wey two fare-plan graphs meet
y-m-25-01.goal: Compare two linear-function fare models and explain with reasons say which one better fit depend on how long people use am.
y-m-25-01.material: The park bike rental station get 2 fare plans. Plan (가) charge starting fare of 1000원, then add 100원 for every minute. Plan (나) no get starting fare and charge 150원 per minute. y-m-25-01.thinking.0: No make general rule from only one example

y-m-25-01.prereq.0: Wetin slope and y-intercept mean in linear function y=ax+b (Grade 8 level)

y-m-25-01.s.s1.st.2.info: This na the fare table on the station notice board. 20 minutes: (가) 3000원, (나) 3000원 / 30 minutes: (가) 4000원, (나) 4500원.

y-m-25-03.title: The equation through both points: we fit trust am?
y-m-25-03.topic: Equation of line through 2 points: independent checking and mistakes in a solution
y-m-25-03.goal: Check whether the check be independent from the information we use to make the equation, find the first wrong line in the solution, and make points on the corrected equation.
y-m-25-03.material: Minsu try to write the line through points A(2, 3) and B(6, 11) on coordinate plane as y=ax+b. The equation Minsu find na y=(1/2)x+2. Minsu say e don finish checking by “put point A(2, 3) inside, (1/2)×2+2=3, so e correct”.
y-m-25-03.thinking.0: Judge the reason for a check
y-m-25-03.prereq.0: Wetin slope a mean in linear function y=ax+b
y-m-25-03.prereq.1: How to check if a point works by putting its coordinates in the equation
y-m-25-03.s.s1.prompt: The equation Minsu find na y=(1/2)x+2 (read: y equals one-half x plus 2), and e say e work when e put point A(2, 3) inside. From this alone, you fit be sure the equation correct? Choose the best judgment.
y-m-25-03.s.s1.hint.0: Remember which of points A and B Minsu likely use, and how, to make the equation.
y-m-25-03.s.s1.hint.1: Think if a check only get meaning when e use information wey no help make the equation.
y-m-25-03.s.s1.o.a: E work for A, so we sure the equation correct and no need check again
y-m-25-03.s.s1.r.a: You no consider if the point wey you use for check overlap with information wey make the equation.
y-m-25-03.s.s1.o.b: A help make the equation, so you suppose put B(6, 11) inside too
y-m-25-03.s.s1.r.b: You think say check get meaning only when e use information wey no help make the equation.
y-m-25-03.s.s1.o.c: E work for A, but e must fail for B, so we suppose throw the equation away
y-m-25-03.s.s1.r.c: You claim say e wrong before even putting B inside.
y-m-25-03.s.s1.explain: E natural say e work for a point wey help make the equation. To know if the equation pass through both points, check with a point we never use yet, or use another method.
y-m-25-03.s.s2.prompt: When B(6, 11) enter, Minsu equation turn out wrong. Choose the first wrong line in Minsu solution (line numbers start from 1, as dem show for screen).
y-m-25-03.s.s2.hint.0: Before you redo every line calculation, work backward from the fact say putting B inside show say e wrong.
y-m-25-03.s.s2.hint.1: Find how much x increase and how much y increase between both points yourself, then compare with line 2.
y-m-25-03.s.s2.line.0: Make the equation of line through A(2, 3) and B(6, 11) be y=ax+b.
y-m-25-03.s.s2.line.1: Slope a = (increase in x) ÷ (increase in y) = (6−2) ÷ (11−3) = 4/8 = 1/2
y-m-25-03.s.s2.line.2: Put A(2, 3) inside y=(1/2)x+b: 3=1+b, so b=2
y-m-25-03.s.s2.line.3: So the equation we want na y=(1/2)x+2
y-m-25-03.s.s2.explain: Na line 2. Slope na (increase in y) ÷ (increase in x), so (11−3) ÷ (6−2)=8/4=2. Lines 3 and 4 follow from the wrong slope. The correct equation na y=2x−1, and if B(6, 11) enter, 12−1=11, correct.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.prompt: Find 3 different points on the correct equation, not A or B, and enter dem as (x, y). But x must be from −10 to 10.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.hint.0: Find how much y increase when x increase by 4 from A to B.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.hint.1: Start from A and find points one by one, using how much y change each time x increase by 1.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.ok.c1: This point dey on the line through A and B.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.fail.c1: This point no dey on the line through A and B. Compare the ratio of x increase to y increase from A to this point with the ratio for AB.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.ok.c2: Na point different from A and B.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.fail.c2: Na same point as A or B. Find another point.
y-m-25-03.s.s3.explain: Example: (0, −1), (1, 1), (4, 7). All dey on y=2x−1. Only one line fit pass through 2 points, so with the correct equation, any x give a point on the same line. Point (4, 4) on Minsu equation y=(1/2)x+2 no dey on this line.

y-m-25-04.title: Even if two equations look different, dem get only one solution?
y-m-25-04.topic: Solutions of simultaneous linear equations and where two lines dey (one solution, none, unlimited)
y-m-25-04.goal: Understand say two linear equations wey look different fit represent the same line, sort cases where number of solutions depend on a constant, and make equations for the same line yourself.
y-m-25-04.material: For simultaneous equations, linear equation ax+by=c fit draw as line on coordinate plane (a and b no be 0 together). If two lines meet at one point, one pair of solutions dey; if dem no meet, no solution; if dem overlap completely, unlimited solutions dey. One pair (x, y) wey satisfy both equations na solution of the simultaneous equations.
y-m-25-04.thinking.0: Separate how e look from wetin e mean
y-m-25-04.thinking.1: State conclusions wey depend on conditions
y-m-25-04.prereq.0: See solutions of linear equation ax+by=c as points on coordinate plane
y-m-25-04.prereq.1: Wetin slope and y-intercept of a line mean
y-m-25-04.s.s1.prompt: How many pairs (x, y) satisfy both first equation 2x−y=−1 (read: 2x minus y equals negative 1) and second equation 4x−2y=−2?
y-m-25-04.s.s1.hint.0: Rewrite each equation as y=(slope)x+(y-intercept), then put dem side by side.
y-m-25-04.s.s1.hint.1: Put x=0 and x=1 inside both equations, find y, and compare.
y-m-25-04.s.s1.o.a: Only one pair dey, because the two equations get different form
y-m-25-04.s.s1.r.a: You think say equations wey look different must be different lines.
y-m-25-04.s.s1.o.b: No pair dey, because both lines get same slope, so dem parallel
y-m-25-04.s.s1.r.b: You look only say the slopes equal and no compare the y-intercepts.
y-m-25-04.s.s1.o.c: Unlimited pairs dey, because both equations represent the same line
y-m-25-04.s.s1.r.c: You see say even if dem look different, both fit be the same line.
y-m-25-04.s.s1.explain: If you divide both sides of 4x−2y=−2 by 2, you get 2x−y=−1. Both equations na the same line, so every point on the line na solution.
y-m-25-04.s.s2.prompt: Keep the first equation as e be, and change the second to 4x−2y=c (c na constant). How the number of solutions change based on c?
y-m-25-04.s.s2.hint.0: Put few values for c, for example −2, 0, 4, and compare the y-intercepts of both lines.
y-m-25-04.s.s2.hint.1: Separate cases where both lines get same slope into same y-intercept and different y-intercept.
y-m-25-04.s.s2.o.a: Whatever c be, unlimited solutions dey because the coefficients same
y-m-25-04.s.s2.r.a: You look only at the equation coefficients and no consider constant c.
y-m-25-04.s.s2.o.b: Only one c give unlimited solutions, and all other values give no solution
y-m-25-04.s.s2.r.b: You see say when c change, the line move parallel.
y-m-25-04.s.s2.o.c: Only one c give no solution, and every other c give one pair
y-m-25-04.s.s2.r.c: You think say when slopes equal, lines must meet in every case.
y-m-25-04.s.s2.o.d: If c no be 0, one pair always dey; if c=0, none dey
y-m-25-04.s.s2.explain: 4x−2y=c mean y=2x−c/2, and the first equation mean y=2x+1. Slopes equal, so both lines na same only when c=−2; for other c dem parallel and no overlap, so no solution.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.prompt: Make second equation ax+by=c wey represent same line as first equation 2x−y=−1. Make the appearance different, so a no fit be 2, and enter 3 different equations as (a, b, c).
y-m-25-04.s.s3.hint.0: Write the first equation coefficients 2, −1, −1 side by side with a, b, c of the second.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.hint.1: Check if the two equations pass through same points when x=0 and when y=0.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.ok.c1: The ratio of x and y coefficients same as first equation, so slope same.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.fail.c1: The ratio of x and y coefficients different from first equation, so slope different.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.ok.c2: The constant term get same ratio too, so both lines overlap.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.fail.c2: The coefficient ratio correct, but constant no follow that ratio, so na different parallel line.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.ok.c3: Its appearance different from first equation.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.fail.c3: a na 2 or 0. Its appearance same as first equation, or e no make a line.
y-m-25-04.s.s3.explain: Example: (4, −2, −2), (−2, 1, 1), (6, −3, −3). If the 3 numbers in second equation na the 3 numbers (2, −1, −1) from first equation multiplied by same number, both equations na same line. If even one number no follow the ratio, no be same line.

y-m-25-05.title: If the slope number bigger, e mean faster?
y-m-25-05.topic: Read slope on graph: compare two graphs with different units
y-m-25-05.goal: Understand say we must read slope together with its units, and convert different units to the same units before comparing two graphs.
y-m-25-05.material: Doyun and Seoa each walk and draw their records as graphs.
